title: TissUExM protocol for ultrastructure expansion microscopy of zebrafish larvae and mouse embryos
protocol: Rehydrate stored embryos in a 2 mL tube at room temperature with orbital agitation.
Incubate embryos in 500 μL of 75% methanol-PBS for 5 minutes.
Incubate embryos in 500 μL of 50% methanol-PBS for 5 minutes.
Incubate embryos in 500 μL of 25% methanol-PBS for 5 minutes.
Incubate embryos in 500 μL PBS for 5 minutes.
Prepare 1 mL of the anchoring solution in a 1.5 mL Epi-tube, aiming for 500 μL per embryo under a fume hood.
Vortex the anchoring solution thoroughly.
Coat a plastic pipette with PBS-Tween 0.1% (PBS-T).
Transfer each embryo to an empty 2 mL tube using the coated pipette.
Remove excess liquid from each embryo.
Add 500 μL of crosslinking solution to each embryo.
Seal each tube containing embryos with parafilm.
Invert each sealed tube multiple times.
Incubate tubes at 37°C for 72 hours.
Gently invert the tubes occasionally during incubation.
Remove the crosslinking solution from embryos under a fume hood.
Rinse embryos three times with 500 μL of PBS-T for 5 minutes each at room temperature with orbital agitation.
Transfer each embryo to a clean 2 mL tube using a plastic pipette coated with PBS-T.
Add 90 μl of inactivated monomer solution (MS) to each tube.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Determine embryo orientation carefully.
Ensure gel integrity during processing.
Prepare the gelation station in advance with all tools ready.
Thaw inactivated MS shortly before use.
Keep the MS tube open during activation.
Vortex between each step during activation.
Place activated solution rapidly onto dried embryos.
Thaw one aliquot of ∼3.5 μL 4OH-TEMPO for two gels.
Thaw one aliquot of ∼3.5 μL TEMED for two gels.
Thaw one aliquot of ∼3.5 μL APS for two gels.
Add PBS and 4OH-TEMPO slowly to the solution.
Add TEMED and APS rapidly to the solution.
Vortex with tube open after adding each component.
Wash embryos carefully before gelation.
Remove the inactivated MS solution from the tubes at 4°C.
Rinse the solution 3 times with 500 μL PBS-T using orbital agitation.
Transfer each embryo onto parafilm in the smallest volume possible using a plastic pipette coated with PBS-T.
Thaw one aliquot of inactivated MS.
Add 3 μL PBS, then vortex.
Add 2 μL 4OH-TEMPO, then vortex.
Add 2.5 μL TEMED, then vortex.
Add 2.5 μL APS, then vortex.
Rapidly remove excess liquid from the embryo.
Add 45 μL of activated gelation solution to each embryo.
Reorient the embryo with a lash if necessary and place it in the center of the drop.
Pop any bubbles that form around the embryo.
Let the embryo stabilize for 5 minutes.
Flip a 12 mm coverslip on each embryo, ensuring it does not slide to the edge.
Replace the coverslip if necessary.
Close the gelation chamber and gently place it at 4°C.
Incubate for 1 hour.
Gently transfer the entire box from 4°C to 37°C.
Incubate for 2 hours.
Place the gel in an Epi-tube containing 1 mL of Collagenase VII diluted in calcium-containing buffer for ZF larvae older than 3 dpf.
Incubate the gel with Collagenase VII for 24 hours at 37°C.
Wash the gel 15 minutes in calcium-containing buffer and another 15 minutes in PBS.
Remove the coverslip gently using forceps.
Add approximately 2 mL of denaturation buffer to a dish or well plate set to 70°C.
Transfer the coverslip and gel to the well containing the denaturation buffer.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature with orbital agitation at 100 rpm.
Using a spatula, transfer each detached gel from its coverslip into a 1.5 mL Epi-tube.
Fill the tube with approximately 1.2 mL of denaturation buffer and add around 100 μL to complete filling the tube.
Incubate at 70°C for 72 hours.
Prepare 35 mm dishes or a 6-well plate with approximately 2 mL of denaturation-like buffer.
Take tubes out of the Thermoblock after incubation.
Using a plastic pipette, gently remove all the denaturation buffer from the bottom of the tube, limiting contact with the gel.
Transfer the gel to the well.
Incubate 15 min at RT at 100 rpm with orbital agitation.
Remove the denaturation-like buffer and add ∼2 mL of PBS.
Incubate 15 min at RT at 100 rpm with orbital agitation.
Pause point: Gels can be stored in PBS at 4°C for a month from now. Consider adding 0.05% sodium azide to prevent contamination.
Prepare a solution of ATTO 647N NHS-ester/PBS (1:2000).
In the gel-containing well, replace PBS with ATTO 647N NHS-ester/PBS.
Protect from light with aluminum foil.
Incubate 2 h at RT at 100 rpm with orbital agitation or 16–72 h at 4°C with optional shaking.
Replace with PBS and verify embryo integrity within the gel, with or without a binocular.
If antibody staining requires a blocking step, perform it along with DAPI labeling for 2 h at room temperature.
Filter the blocking solution through a 0.45 μm filter and keep at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Prepare a solution of DAPI/PBS (1:2000).
In the gel-containing well, replace PBS with DAPI/PBS.
Protect from light using aluminum foil during incubation.
Incubate for 2 h at room temperature with orbital agitation at 100 rpm.
Replace DAPI/PBS with PBS after incubation.
Measure the gel diameter; it should consistently be between 26-30 mm.
Optionally place the gel in an Attofluor chamber with a 24 mm coverslip if controlled is performed with an epifluorescence microscope.
Optional: If antibody concentration or cost is a limiting factor, trim the gel to fit in a smaller well (2 mL in a 6-well plate, 1 mL in a 12-well plate).
Gels can be stored in PBS at 4°C and protected from light for up to 2 weeks.
Transfer individual gels to a 6-well plate or individual 2 mL tubes.
Incubate each gel in 2 mL PBS-BSA 2% with primary antibodies at 37°C for 4 days with orbital agitation.
Wash each gel 3 times with PBS-T for 45 minutes at room temperature and 100 rpm.
Incubate each gel in 2 mL PBS-BSA 2% with secondary antibodies at 37°C for 3 days with orbital agitation.
Wash each gel 3 times with PBS-T for 45 minutes at room temperature and 100 rpm.
Replace the last washing solution with 2 mL of PBS.
Mount set up on a plastic box covered with parafilm and Attofluor chamber.
Use plastic scalpels and spatula for gel handling.
Blot excess water from the gel using Kimwipe.
Immerse the gel in water, measure when fully expanded.
Trim the gel to obtain a rectangle of approximately 12–15 mm.
Measure the new size after trimming for future calculation of expansion factor.
Store gels in PBS at 4°C and protected from light for up to 2 weeks if not used immediately.
Transfer each trimmed gel into a container with an excess of water.
Incubate the gel in water for 1 hour at room temperature, protected from light.
Replace the water after the initial incubation.
Continue incubating between 1 hour and 16 hours, preferably overnight, protected from light.
Replace the water one last time.
Incubate for 1 hour.
Place the gel on parafilm and measure its final size.
Rehydrate the gel with a few drops of water if it becomes opaque or porous during transfer steps.
Mount the gel in an Attofluor chamber using PDL-coated coverslips.
Dry the gel on a Kimwipe using a spatula.
Remove as much water as possible from the gel.
Place the dried gel in the chamber.
Press gently if air bubbles are present between the coverslip and the gel.
Trim the corners of the gel if necessary to close the chamber.
Add 1–2 drops of water on top of the gel.
Make sure the gel stays hydrated by adding a drop of water every ∼30 minutes during imaging.
Rehydrate the gel if it shows signs of dehydration, such as sudden drift or fluorescent increase.
Wait 5 minutes after rehydration for the gel to stabilize before continuing imaging.
Use a pipet to add water between the gel and coverslip when detaching the gel.
Be gentle while detaching the gel to avoid breaking it.
